questions.q: How does item-level sharing differ from giving someone workspace access?
options: They are the same thing, just accessed from different menus
Item-level sharing hands one report or dashboard to someone, who may have no broader workspace access at all
Item-level sharing can only be used by workspace Admins
Workspace access only applies to dashboards, never reports
questions.explain: Workspace access (Lesson 3) grants a role across everything in a workspace. Item-level sharing is narrower — handing one specific item to someone who may have no other access to that workspace.

questions.q: In the Send link dialog, what does the top link-type selector actually control?
options: The file format the report downloads as
Who can use the link at all — people in the org, specific people, or people with existing access
Whether the report refreshes automatically
The sensitivity label applied to the item
questions.explain: The link-type selector is the real access control in the dialog — it determines who can use the link before any individual names are even entered.

questions.q: What do the 'Allow recipients to share this item' and 'Allow recipients to build content' toggles control?
options: Whether the report can be downloaded as a PDF
The dashboard's refresh schedule
Resharing further, and letting recipients build new reports off the same underlying data, respectively
Whether Row-Level Security applies to the recipient
questions.explain: Resharing lets recipients pass the link along further; build permission lets them create new content using the same semantic model's data. Both are governance-relevant toggles worth checking explicitly.

questions.q: Why is Manage permissions, rather than Send link, the screen to use when auditing an item's access?
options: Send link cannot be used more than once per item
Manage permissions lists every link and direct share already granted, with the ability to revoke each one
Manage permissions is only visible to tenant administrators
Send link and Manage permissions show identical information
questions.explain: Send link only grants access going forward. Manage permissions is the audit view — everything already shared, and a way to revoke any of it.

questions.q: According to this lesson's governance guidance, what link type should be the default choice?
options: Always 'People in your organization,' since it's the simplest option
The narrowest link type that still accomplishes the goal, such as 'Specific people' over organization-wide
Always 'People with existing access,' regardless of the situation
There is no meaningful difference between link types for governance purposes
questions.explain: Defaulting to the narrowest link type that still works reduces unnecessary exposure — organization-wide links are convenient but also the easiest to forget about and the broadest in reach.
